title: A High Sample Median
problem: Three independent numbers are drawn uniformly from [0,1]. What is the probability their median exceeds 3/4?

hints.text: The median exceeds 3/4 exactly when at least two of the three observations exceed 3/4.
Each observation exceeds 3/4 with probability 1/4; count two or three successes.

solution.setup: Let a success be a draw above 3/4. The number of successes is Binomial(3,1/4).
solution.reasoning: The median is above 3/4 when there are at least two successes. The probability is C(3,2)(1/4)²(3/4)+(1/4)³=9/64+1/64=10/64.
solution.sanityCheck: The event is uncommon because two high observations are required, but it is more likely than all three being high, which alone has probability 1/64.

keyInsight: Translate an order-statistic event into a count of observations above a threshold.
recognitionCues: A statement about a sample median can often be rewritten as requiring a certain number of threshold exceedances.
commonMistakes: Requiring all three draws to exceed 3/4.
followUps: Find the probability the median lies between 1/4 and 3/4.
